sentences: [3] Elections in the 2000s In the 2001 Bangladeshi general election held on 1 October 2001, Sardar Shakhawat Hossain Bokul of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) won the Narsingdi-4 constituency, defeating the Awami League (AL) candidate with a margin reflecting the BNP-led alliance's national landslide of 193 seats out of 300.

[42] Elections in the 2010s In the 2014 Bangladeshi general election, held on 5 January amid a boycott by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and its allies, Awami League candidate Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun was elected as the Member of Parliament for Narsingdi-4, securing victory in a contest with limited opposition participation.

Electoral History Overview of Electoral Trends The Narsingdi-4 constituency, encompassing parts of Narsingdi District, exhibited competitive electoral dynamics in the 1990s and early 2000s, with the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) securing victories in the 1991 and 2001 general elections.

[3] [4] In 2005, during the 8th Jatiya Sangsad, a by-election was held for Narsingdi-4 following the death of the incumbent MP, with Khairul Kabir Khokon elected on a Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) nomination.

[33] Prior to Humayun's dominance, the constituency saw representation by figures from the Bangladesh Nationalist Party during the 8th Jatiya Sangsad (2001–2006), reflecting earlier alternations between major parties amid competitive elections.

[63] Political parties ramped up grassroots preparations, with the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) announcing nominations for candidates in four of Narsingdi's five constituencies, including potential contenders for Narsingdi-4, emphasizing a 31-point agenda for economic equity.

[19] Historical Context Formation of the Constituency Narsingdi-4 was established as a single-member parliamentary constituency within the framework of Bangladesh's 300 territorial seats for the Jatiya Sangsad, with its formation tied to administrative realignments after Narsingdi district's separation in 1984 from Dhaka and Mymensingh districts.

[3] [4] Notable Representatives and Their Tenures Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun, affiliated with the Bangladesh Awami League, represented Narsingdi-4 as Member of Parliament for five consecutive terms spanning the 9th through 12th Jatiya Sangsad, from his initial election on 29 December 2008 until the parliament's dissolution on 6 August 2024.
[38] Elections in the 2020s The general election for Narsingdi-4 was held on 7 January 2024 as part of Bangladesh's nationwide parliamentary polls.

Awami League candidate Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun, the incumbent Industries Minister, won the seat for a fourth consecutive term, defeating challengers in a contest marked by the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party's (BNP) boycott.

[49] Elections Prior to 2000 The parliamentary constituency of Narsingdi-4 participated in Bangladesh's general elections of 1973, 1979, 1986, 1988, 1991, and 1996, each conducted under varying political conditions including military rule and democratic transitions.

Detailed constituency-level data, including vote tallies and margins for Narsingdi-4, are preserved in Bangladesh Election Commission reports, which indicate alignment with national shifts driven by local patronage networks and party mobilization in Belabo and Monohardi upazilas.

[59] Preparations for Upcoming Elections The Election Commission of Bangladesh announced the schedule for the 13th National Parliamentary Election on December 11, 2025, with voting set for February 12, 2026, marking the first national polls since the 2024 uprising that led to the vacancy in Narsingdi-4.

[68] No widespread allegations of irregularities were substantiated in prior elections specific to Narsingdi-4, though national patterns of vote stuffing and intimidation have been reported in Bangladeshi polls since 2014, often linked to ruling party dominance.
[2] The constituency has consistently returned candidates from the Bangladesh Awami League in elections from 2008 to 2024.
[6] Geography and Boundaries Administrative Boundaries Narsingdi-4 is a parliamentary constituency within Narsingdi District, situated in the Dhaka Division of Bangladesh.
The initial election occurred on 7 May 1986, integrating the area into national representation under the unicameral parliament's structure of 300 directly elected members.
[26] A pivotal shift occurred in 1984 with the creation of Narsingdi District from Mymensingh District and the nationwide introduction of the upazila system under the military regime of H.M.

[30] Political Representation List of Members of Parliament Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun served as the Member of Parliament for Narsingdi-4 in multiple terms, beginning with his election as an independent candidate in 1986 during the 3rd Jatiya Sangsad.

[31] He was re-elected in the 9th Jatiya Sangsad (2009–2014), 10th Jatiya Sangsad (2014–2018), 11th Jatiya Sangsad (2018–2024), and 12th Jatiya Sangsad following the general election on 7 January 2024, marking his fifth term overall and representing the Bangladesh Awami League in these later parliaments.
[3] Term Member of Parliament Party Election Year/Notes 3rd Jatiya Sangsad (1986–1988) Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun Independent Elected 7 May 1986.
[34] No other representatives from Narsingdi-4 have achieved comparable national prominence or ministerial roles in recent decades.
These outcomes aligned with BNP's national surge, capturing 140 seats in 1991 and 193 in 2001 amid relatively high voter participation and multiparty contests.

Humayun was re-elected unopposed in the 2014 election, boycotted by the BNP-led opposition, and secured victories in 2018 with over 256,000 votes against BNP challenger Sardar Shakhawat Hossain Bokul, as well as in 2024 for his fourth term overall.

[3] These elections highlighted partisan swings in Narsingdi-4, mirroring national polarization between BNP and AL, with no independent or minor party breakthroughs in the constituency during the decade.

In Narsingdi district, encompassing the Narsingdi-4 constituency, unrest peaked on 19 July 2024 when protesters stormed the district jail amid a nationwide curfew, freeing over 850 inmates—many held on political charges—and setting the facility ablaze before fleeing with weapons from the armory.

The following day, 6 August 2024, President Mohammed Shahabuddin dissolved the Jatiya Sangsad (National Parliament) at the request of student leaders, vacating all 300 constituency seats, including Narsingdi-4.

[73] Studies on Bangladeshi electoral dynamics indicate that such shifts from governing-party control often reduce targeted public spending in affected constituencies, leading to measurable declines in household consumption and poverty alleviation efforts previously directed by incumbent MPs.

[73] Conversely, student-led groups and BNP strategists highlight the shift's role in curbing pre-electoral violence historically linked to ruling-party muscle in constituencies like Narsingdi-4, where past national dominance enabled systematic intimidation of rivals.
Nurul Majid Mahmud Humayun, an Awami League politician and lawyer, served as MP for Narsingdi-4 for five terms, most recently elected in 2024.
[3] [4] During his tenure, Humayun served as Minister of Industries from 2019 to 2024, overseeing policies for the sector amid Bangladesh's rapid industrialization.

[8] [9] [10] The boundaries of Narsingdi-4 were subject to redrawing as part of the Election Commission's nationwide delimitation process finalized on 4 September 2025, aimed at achieving compactness, administrative feasibility, and equitable voter distribution averaging around 420,000 per constituency based on recent census data.

[11] Physical and Economic Geography Narsingdi-4 occupies flat, low-lying alluvial plains characteristic of central Bangladesh's Bengal delta region, with terrain primarily consisting of fertile floodplains susceptible to annual inundation.
[13] [14] Demographics Population Statistics The Narsingdi-4 parliamentary constituency comprises Belabo Upazila and Monohardi Upazila in Narsingdi District.

Poverty dynamics in the district align with national trends, with sub-district variations addressed through model-based estimations in recent mappings, though specific upazila-level headcount rates for Narsingdi-4 remain tied to broader district assessments showing rural-urban disparities.

[32] As Minister of Industries from 2019 onward, Humayun oversaw policies aimed at industrial growth, including support for small and medium enterprises through institutions like the Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industries Corporation.

[3] [4] This AL dominance mirrors national patterns of one-party sweeps in recent cycles, often marred by opposition abstention, reports of irregularities, and depressed turnout—such as cancellations in specific polling stations during the 2024 vote due to alleged malpractices.

[36] Overall, the trends reflect a transition from bipolar competition to AL hegemony post-2008, influenced by incumbency advantages, caretaker government abolition in 2011 favoring the ruling party, and localized factors like Humayun's longstanding influence as a lawyer and minister.

[3] The election occurred amid widespread allegations of pre-poll violence, voter intimidation, and ballot stuffing, with international observers and opposition figures questioning its fairness; official turnout was reported at around 40% nationally, though local figures for Narsingdi-4 were not independently verified beyond government announcements.
[39] Humayun's victory extended Awami League dominance in the constituency, consistent with prior trends, but the parliament formed from these results lasted only seven months.

sentences: ‘No Place for Corrupt, Criminals, Land Grabbers or Extortionists in BNP’: Health Minister Sardar Sakhawat Hossain Bakul Health and Family Welfare Minister and Narsingdi-4 (Monohardi-Belabo) MP Sardar Sakhawat Hossain Bakul has said there will be no place in the party for corrupt individuals, criminals, land grabbers, extortionists or people involved in armed activities.
Sardar Sakhawat Hossain Bakul said his government responsibilities and organizational activities often prevent him from staying in the constituency regularly.

At the conclusion of the meeting, Sardar Sakhawat Hossain Bakul urged party leaders and activists to rise above personal interests, maintain party discipline and work for the welfare of ordinary people.

The minister strongly warned party leaders and activists against allegations of land grabbing, particularly involving vulnerable and helpless people, as well as other irregularities at the local level.
“No injustice will be tolerated,” he said, urging party workers to avoid using personal influence to secure advantages or engaging in politics aimed at pleasing different sides.
He stressed that holding a party position alone is not enough.
He also warned against extortion, terrorism, corruption and misconduct, saying such activities directly damage the party's image.
Party leaders were also asked to increase publicity of the programs on social media and install posters and banners across their respective unions and local areas.

The minister emphasized transparency in the distribution of Family Cards, saying the cards must reach genuinely eligible beneficiaries rather than being distributed on the basis of party affiliation or personal recommendations.
Bakul also urged party members to maintain cordial relations with ordinary citizens and help preserve a democratic political environment.
The minister asked local party leaders to remain vigilant over allegations that some fertilizer dealers may be hoarding supplies.
